_what_this_is: The one place that says whether a finding from the 7 September 2026 audit is still open. Every other status record in docs/audits/ is a SNAPSHOT taken on a date and never updated; this one is amended in the same commit that closes a finding. Read _how_to_read before using it.

_how_to_read.closed: verified against the code, by a human read, on verified_on. The defect is gone.
_how_to_read.not_a_defect: the premise was false, or the suggested fix would be worse than the defect. The reason is recorded.
_how_to_read.open: verified against the code and still true.
_how_to_read.blocked: cannot be closed by code alone — it needs a registration, a state notification, or a figure only a person holds.
_how_to_read.unverified: not re-read since the date named. Treat as unknown, NOT as open.
_how_to_read.closed_by_commit: named in a merged commit AND in an in-code comment that says what it closed. Two independent traces; not a re-read.
_how_to_read.closed_by_commit_only: named in a merged commit and nowhere else. The weakest state in this file — read these before quoting them as done.
_how_to_read.partial: verified against the code: part of the finding is fixed and part is still true. `why` says which part is closed and `what_is_left` says what is not. Never quote one of these as done.

GST-20.why: CLOSED. Migration 390 adds public.client_gst_registrations and — the structural half — narrows the unique key on BOTH return tables from (client_id, period) to (client_id, period, gstin). That constraint is the finding: CGST Act s.25(1) requires registration in every State a taxable supply is made from and s.25(2)'s proviso allows one per place of business within a state, but a client with two registrations could not have held two June returns between them WHATEVER the code did, so the CA's only route was a second fake 'client' per GSTIN — which then splits the accounting of one legal person across two ledgers and breaks every client-scoped report. domain/gst/registrations.py is the authority; services/client_gst_registration_service.py fetches and writes; routers/client_gst_registrations.py and the client GST screen's Registrations tab decide nothing. clients.gstin IS NOT REPLACED and that is deliberate: it stays the PRIMARY and the table holds the ADDITIONAL ones only. Making it a cache of a table-held primary was rejected because a cache needs one write path and that column already has several (onboarding, the client edit screen, migration 073's seed), so it would drift the first time somebody edited a client and surface as a return filed under the wrong registration; there is no backfill for the same reason. A GSTIN THE CLIENT DOES NOT HOLD IS REFUSED, NEVER DEFAULTED — in the domain module and again as a 422 in the service — because filing one registration's return under another's number is invisible until the portal rejects it or, worse, accepts it; and the PRIMARY COMES FIRST for the mirror reason, since a screen opens on [0] and that must be the registration every existing document already carries. The narrowed key made _existing_return load-bearing: a save path still matching on (client, period) alone would now find the OTHER registration's return and revise it, silently replacing one state's figures with another's, so the GSTIN is a required parameter there with no default and the mock branch matches it too. files_gstr1_and_3b keeps every caller from testing the type by name — a composition dealer files CMP-08 and GSTR-4 under s.10, an ISD GSTR-6, a s.51 deductor GSTR-7, a s.52 operator GSTR-8, and OTHER_RETURN_FORMS holds the sentence so a refusal names the form that registration actually owes; an SEZ unit, an SEZ developer, a casual and a non-resident DO file the ordinary pair. state_code is DERIVED from the GSTIN's first two characters and never taken from the caller (the column CHECKs state_code = left(gstin, 2)), taking the PREFIX rather than gstin.state_code for place_of_supply's reason. Shape and check digit delegate to domain/gst/gstin.problem_with — there is one implementation of that and this is not a second. Closing is not deleting: a s.29 cancellation sets effective_to, because the returns for every period the registration was live are still owed and the rows filed under it are keyed on its GSTIN; withdraw is for a registration recorded in error and is refused once any return exists under it. Writes are rbac('client', 'write') rather than a GST action, because clients.gstin — the primary — is written under exactly that, and a GST action would let an Executive who may COMPUTE a return also add the registration it is filed under while being unable to correct the primary beside it. RLS on, assignment-scope RESTRICTIVE policy, SELECT-only to authenticated. 41/41 negative controls after two tests were added: one mutating the service to fall back to the primary instead of 422ing, and one mutating the mock lookup to ignore the GSTIN without changing the source the guard reads. ONE DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THIS WORK'S OWN NEW TEST AND IS FIXED IN THE SAME MIGRATION: `gstr3b_returns.gstin` is NULLABLE — 036's CREATE TABLE omitted the column and migration 234 added it as a bare TEXT — and Postgres treats NULLs as DISTINCT in a unique index, so (client_id, period, gstin) would have enforced NOTHING on a row saved without one. Narrowing the key would have REMOVED the protection UNIQUE (client_id, period) gave those rows rather than refining it. 390 therefore back-fills both return tables' NULL gstin from clients.gstin BEFORE dropping the old constraint (that constraint is what guarantees at most one row per (client, period), so the update cannot collide; and before 390 a client held exactly one registration, so clients.gstin IS the registration such a row was prepared under — a repair of 234's omission, not a guess), and keys both indexes on coalesce(gstin, '') so a row that still has none is constrained exactly as before. No SET NOT NULL: merging applies this to production with no review step, and one unbackfillable row would abort the deploy and block every later migration. The test is written as the RULE — two returns with no registration recorded, one client, one period, must be refused — so it holds whichever way a later migration closes it.

PUR-19.why: CLOSED. Migration 388 adds public.rcm_documents and vendors.gst_registration_status; domain/gst/rcm_documents.py is the authority and decides everything, the router and the screen decide nothing. THE TWO SECTIONS ARE NOT ONE RULE WITH TWO NAMES, which is the whole of this finding: CGST Act s.31(3)(f) makes the RECIPIENT issue a self-invoice only on a reverse-charge supply received from a supplier who is NOT REGISTERED, while s.31(3)(g) makes them issue a payment voucher at the time of payment on EVERY s.9(3)/(4) liability, registered supplier or not — so a payment to a REGISTERED goods transport agency owes a voucher and owes no self-invoice, and asking the registration question in payment_voucher_due would import (f)'s limb into a section that does not carry it. The self-invoice is the document the input credit RESTS on (Rule 36(1)(b) with s.16(2)(a)), so it is not paperwork. REGISTRATION HAS THREE STATES AND THE THIRD IS REFUSED, NOT GUESSED: a valid GSTIN on the vendor IS the registration (read through domain/gst/gstin.problem_with, so a malformed one reports itself rather than being read as registered), vendors.gst_registration_status answers it where there is no GSTIN, and NULL is unrecorded — named as a gap, because one guess mints a document the Act does not ask for and the other withholds the one the credit rests on. The column is nullable with NO DEFAULT and CHECKed to the two settled answers, so 'unrecorded' cannot be STORED as a string; both API doors (VendorIn and VendorUpdateIn) normalise case and refuse it with a sentence saying it is the absence of a value, and both the client Vendors tab and the firm-level Supplier Master serve the picker from GET /api/rcm-documents/registration-states rather than spelling the pair. A DECISION'S `reasons` AND `gaps` ARE DIFFERENT THINGS and the panel renders them differently: reasons mean the Act does not ask for the document (settled), gaps mean nobody can yet tell (actionable). The particulars are built in the domain module rather than in a PDF, so the JSON the endpoint serves and the document the CA prints are one object. Four refusals are recorded rather than guessed: no consolidated month-end self-invoice ([S], tied to the withdrawn Notification 8/2017-CT(R)); whether s.9(4) applies is the bill's own is_reverse_charge, which is the CA's answer and not re-decided here; a cancelled registration is not modelled; and Rule 46(h)'s UQC is absent because purchase_bill_lines has no unit column — named, never invented. Issuing asks BOTH period questions and validates the number against Rule 46(b) through the one domain/gst/invoice_series authority; the table's uniqueness is per client PER KIND (Rule 46(b) allows one or multiple series and these are two), one document per parent, partial on deleted_at so a document issued in error can be withdrawn and reissued, RLS on with an assignment-scope RESTRICTIVE policy and SELECT-only to authenticated so every write runs rbac(). 16/16 negative controls on the domain suite and the browser guard, plus 2/2 on the model door.

PUR-25.why: CLOSED. Migration 393 adds purchase_orders / _lines and goods_receipt_notes / _lines, plus a nullable link from a bill line back to the order line it is for; domain/purchases/order_cycle.py is the commercial chain and domain/purchases/three_way_match.py is the comparison; services/purchase_cycle_service.py fetches and writes; routers/purchase_cycle.py serves it; the client Purchases screen's new 'Orders & Goods Receipts' tab renders it and decides nothing. THE FINDING NAMES A CONTROL AND THE ABSENCE WAS STATUTORY. The familiar reason to compare order, receipt and bill is that it stops a bill being paid for goods nobody received or at a price nobody agreed — both real. But in an Indian practice the comparison also settles two questions nothing else in the books can answer. CGST s.16(2)(b) allows the input tax credit only where the recipient HAS RECEIVED the goods, and a March invoice for goods arriving in April carries credit belonging to April; nothing recorded receipt at all, so the condition could not be tested. And MSMED s.15 runs its fifteen days from ACCEPTANCE, which s.2(b)'s Explanation makes the day of ACTUAL DELIVERY — so domain/income_tax/section_43b_h.py had to use the BILL date as a proxy and carried ACCEPTANCE_DATE_NOT_HELD on EVERY answer. The proxy is the EARLIER date and therefore the LARGER disallowance, so it manufactured add-backs on bills paid in time. A goods receipt supplies the real date, the caveat is now emitted only for the bills that actually fell back, and each bill's working says which date it measured from. IT REPORTS AND NEVER BLOCKS A BILL: a supplier who short-ships has still sent one and the CA still has to book what arrived — refusing would push the entry outside the system, which is worse than a mismatch nobody looked at. The one refusal is an over-RECEIPT against the order, because goods on the premises in excess of what was ordered mean the ORDER is wrong, and clamping would take the ordered quantity in and lose the rest with no record of stock that physically exists. NO TOLERANCE IS APPLIED AND NONE IS INVENTED — 'within 2%' is a firm's procurement policy rather than a rule, and a tolerance would silently pass a discrepancy somebody has to see; every answer carries the sentence saying so, and the browser guard refuses a filter on the differences list. NO PRICE VARIANCE IS POSTED: INV-05a costs a receipt at the BILL's own taxable value plus its s.17(5)-blocked tax, so the bill IS the cost and a variance account would double-count. A BILL WITH NO ORDER IS NOT A FINDING, because most purchases a practice sees — fees, rent, utilities — are never ordered, and reporting each as unmatched would bury the ones that matter. The first proviso to s.16(2) ('bill to ship to') is NAMED rather than modelled: whether an arrangement is one is a fact about the contract that no column holds, so an order with no receipt is reported rather than treated as an unmet condition. NEITHER DOCUMENT POSTS A JOURNAL OR MOVES STOCK — the expense, the credit and the payable all arise when the bill is received — and two tests assert it, one walking the service's AST (not its raw source, which a docstring naming the forbidden symbol would satisfy) and one that no return builder reads any of the four tables. Goods received and not invoiced are a real accrual; building it needs a GRNI account and a reversal path and is named as an owner decision rather than half-built. `rejected_qty` IS ITS OWN FIGURE rather than a smaller quantity, because s.16(2)(b) asks what was RECEIVED and s.2(b) what was ACCEPTED and one number cannot answer both; what the order still owes is measured on what was KEPT. The acceptance date is the LAST receipt and not the first — a part-shipped order is accepted when the goods the bill covers have all arrived — and an objection REMOVED (s.2(b)'s second limb) displaces it, which is LATER and so can only remove a disallowance, never create one; the database CHECKs the objection pair's order and both API doors refuse a removal with no objection behind it. The YEAR of the add-back is still the BILL's: s.43B(h) disallows a deduction claimed in the year the expense ACCRUED in, so only the fifteen-day clock moves — a March bill received in April must not slide its disallowance into the next year. What an order still has open is DERIVED, never stored (migration 278's reasoning applied to a quantity), read `.in_` over that order's own line ids with each row's PARENT status checked, because a cancelled receipt has received nothing. 36 backend negative controls (23 on the engines and the service, 2 on the parent-scoping guard, 11 already covered by the shared cases) and 13 in the browser, all caught. TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THIS COMMIT'S OWN CODE WERE FOUND BY THE RATCHETS, not by the tests: `purchase_bill_lines` has NO firm_id column — it is scoped through its parent bill — so the billed-quantity read named a column production does not have, which is PGRST204 and NO read, leaving the figure silently nil; and the firm-filter guard needed a named exemption for exactly that table plus a second test that the PARENT read still carries the filter, so the two guards cannot both be satisfied by dropping the tenant check altogether. MAX_UNREADABLE 455 -> 457 for the two genuinely dynamic PATCH payloads, with the reason in the file.

DRAFTS ONLY — receiving is what posts Dr Expense / Dr GST Input / Cr Trade Payables, withholds the TDS and claims the credit, and stays the CA's act. The tax is the ordinary bill engine's, not this module's. ONE CADENCE ENGINE: domain/recurrence is imported, and a test asserts the module holds no copy — two engines drifting means one feature generates in a month the other skips. A FAILED occurrence is recorded and the template does NOT advance. `bill_no` is the VENDOR'S own number and is left blank (it is half the key GSTR-2B matching uses); `our_reference` is stamped. PUR-26.why_it_mattered_more_here: Most of the s.194 series charges on the YEAR'S AGGREGATE (s.194C(5) and the 'aggregate of the sums' limb in ss.194A/194D/194G/194H/194J), so a month nobody entered does not only lose an expense — it changes what the NEXT bill should withhold, and with it the Rule 30(2) deposit and the quarterly statement.

SALES-21.why: CLOSED. Migration 392 adds six tables — sales_quotations / _lines, sales_orders / _lines and delivery_challans / _lines; domain/sales/order_cycle.py is the commercial chain and domain/gst/delivery_challan.py is CGST Rule 55; services/sales_cycle_service.py fetches and writes; routers/sales_cycle.py serves it; the client Sales screen's new 'Quotes, Orders & Challans' tab renders it and decides nothing. THE FINDING IS THE WHOLE OF IT: the cycle started at the tax invoice, so a CA either raised it EARLY — declaring a supply that had not happened and paying tax on it a month before the money arrived — or kept the quotation in a spreadsheet and re-typed every line when it converted. THREE OF THE FOUR DOCUMENTS ARE COMMERCIAL AND THE ACT DOES NOT KNOW THEM: CGST s.7 charges a SUPPLY and an offer is not one, so no table carries a journal_entry_id, nothing posts, nothing moves stock, and two tests assert it — one on the service's AST (not its raw source: the first draft failed on the module's own docstring, which NAMES _create_journal to say it is not imported) and one that no return builder reads any of the six tables. The proforma invoice is the trap: it looks like an invoice, is often numbered like one, and a GSTR-1 that picked one up would declare a supply that never happened. It is NEVER numbered from the tax-invoice series — Rule 46(b) requires that series to be CONSECUTIVE and unique for the FY, so consuming a number for a document that may never become a supply leaves a permanent gap and reusing it later puts two documents on one number. Uniqueness is per client PER KIND, so a quotation and a proforma may share a number and two quotations may not. THE DELIVERY CHALLAN IS THE ACT'S AND IS WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. Two of Rule 55's movements start a clock whose expiry is a DEEMED SUPPLY: s.143(3) deems inputs not received back within ONE YEAR to have been supplied to the job worker ON THE DAY THEY WERE SENT OUT — so the tax falls due in a return already filed, with s.50(1) interest from that return's own due date — s.143(4) is the same at THREE years for capital goods, and s.31(7) gives goods sent on approval SIX MONTHS from removal. Neither clock is visible in any ledger: the goods left, nothing was billed, no journal moved. The challan is the only document either can be computed from, which is the point of the module rather than a convenience, and the screen opens on the overdue count. goods_kind IS NULLABLE WITH NO DEFAULT AND IS REFUSED, NEVER GUESSED — defaulting to inputs reports a deemed supply two years early and defaulting to capital goods hides one for two years, while moulds, dies, jigs, fixtures and tools are outside both (second proviso to s.143(1)) and are NAMED as their own answer, because 'no clock' and 'a clock nobody computed' must not look the same on a screen. Two CHECKs keep a kind of goods and a Commissioner's extension on a job-work movement only, and an extension is honoured only where it is LATER than the statutory date. A month-end deadline walks BACK to the month's last day (31 August plus six months is 28 February, or 29 in a leap year), never forward, because forward is a day late on a deemed supply. RULE 55(1)'S NINE CLAUSES ARE CHECKED AND TWO ARE CONDITIONAL: (vii) tax rate and amount only 'where the transportation is for supply to the consignee' — a job-work despatch carries none, and the SERVICE zeroes the rate rather than asking the caller to remember, because that is a rule a caller will get wrong — and (viii) place of supply only on an inter-State movement. Rule 55(2)'s three legends are verbatim, because the rule prescribes the WORDS. A partial HSN answer reports as ABSENT (the officer reads line by line) while a nil TAX reports as '0', which is a real answer on an exempt or nil-rated supply. WHAT AN ORDER STILL HAS OPEN IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED — migration 278's reasoning applied to a quantity — from challan lines read .in_ over THIS order's line ids and their PARENTS' statuses, since a cancelled challan has delivered nothing and a query that forgot it would show goods delivered that never left and then refuse the real delivery as an over-delivery. THE ONE FACT THIS PRODUCT CANNOT HOLD IS WHETHER THE SUPPLIER FILED, and it is NAMED on every answer rather than guessed. BANK-24.why: Closed under the owner's own scope, and the investigation moved the defect. The per-transaction control the owner described already existed — EntryDetailModal's "GST inside this amount" rate select plus the inter-state toggle, gated on `gst_allowed`, sent by pass() — and bank_posting_service already split the tax-inclusive amount and posted a real Dr GST Input leg. What was missing was the other end: GSTR-3B is built from DOCUMENTS (purchase bills, the two purchase note types, sales invoices, the §34 notes) and a bank line is none of them, so the credit the CA had declared never reached Table 4(A) — while _gl_gst_movements DID read the GST Input account, so the same rupees came back as an unexplained books-vs-ledger ITC difference, every month, on a return about to be filed. Money IN was the same defect and worse: build_inclusive_lines(is_credit=True) credits GST Output, so an outward supply's liability sat in the ledger and no return declared it. Migration 382 records the POSTED rate on bank_transactions (the draft cannot serve — the caller may override it, and a line posted with no draft carries NULL), so the TRANSACTION is the document and the reconciliation's two sides stay independently derived. domain/gst/bank_charge_gst.py is the rule; gstr3b_from_books feeds the inward side to 4(A)(5) "All other ITC" and the outward side to 3.1(a) through the one _outward_transactions Rule 43's turnover also reads. Three refusals are deliberate and named: a recorded ZERO declares nothing (it posts identically to an unmarked line, so the books cannot say whether a receipt is nil-rated, exempt, outside the levy, or not a supply at all); an outward bank line never reaches Table 3.2 (no recipient state, no recipient class); and no §17(5) split. The two facts that cannot be computed are NAMED on every answer that carries one — §16(2)(aa) wants a supplier document a bank line does not hold, and an outward supply with no tax invoice will not be in the GSTR-1 the portal compares this return against (Rule 46). No GSTIN is invented, which is what the finding's own suggested fix would have done.

TDS-23.why: s.194T IS IN THE REGISTRY. The Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 inserted it with effect from 01-04-2025 — this registry's own FIRST year, whose header claims that Act — so its absence was a hole in a verified year, and every partnership and LLP client has the obligation. It reached the CA as the bare string "Unknown TDS section '194T'" at the first bill, long after the vendor master had saved it silently. 10% with BOTH limbs at ₹20,000, and `SECTION_194T_FIRST_FY` names the commencement rather than leaving it implicit in which years the dict happens to hold. A THIRD residency state came with it: s.194T's words carry no resident limb, so it cannot join RESIDENT_ONLY_SECTIONS (whose every entry quotes the limitation it is listed for), and putting it in SECTIONS_REACHING_NON_RESIDENTS would assert that 10% flat on a 27Q row is right when s.195 charges the rates in force with surcharge and cess and no threshold. `SECTIONS_UNSETTLED_FOR_A_NON_RESIDENT` refuses it against a non-resident with the reason, asked BEFORE the resident-only lookup because falling through reaches the deliberate silence for unclassified sections and would allow the deduction. s.194R is refused with ITS two reasons rather than a bare 'no rate held': whether the Finance Act 2025 moved its ₹20,000 could not be confirmed here, and the benefit is often in KIND, a base no bill line holds. THE LAST THREE ARE ANSWERED NOW, each with its own sentence rather than the bare string "Unknown TDS section" a CA used to get at the first bill. §194N is a DIRECTION refusal like §206C: it is charged on a banking company, a co-operative bank or a post office on cash the ACCOUNT HOLDER withdraws, so on a bill this client is paying there is nothing to withhold — when it bites the client is the DEDUCTEE and the credit appears in their Form 26AS, which is where the refusal sends them. Saying only 'no rate held' would have invited somebody to add one. §194O is refused on its BASE: the gross amount of the PARTICIPANT'S sale is not a bill the operator receives and is in no purchase ledger, and its rate moved part-way through FY 2024-25 by the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 without that being confirmable here. §194S is refused because there is no virtual-digital-asset transfer document to compute on, its rate and its two thresholds are unconfirmed, and §194S(2) requires the tax paid before consideration in kind is released — a base no bill line holds. The one-section set became a DICT of per-section reasons: what a CA has to go and do differs per section, and one shared paragraph would have said the wrong thing about two of the three — asserted as such, on the answers rather than on the data, so moving a reason in or out cannot make the test vacuous. 6/6 negative controls.
